overview: PSEG is a New Jersey-based public utility holding company operating through two segments: PSE&G, a regulated electric and gas transmission and distribution (T&D) utility serving 2.4 million electric and 1.9 million gas customers across the most densely populated parts of New Jersey, and PSEG Power, a merchant nuclear generation business that owns Salem 1 & 2, Hope Creek and a 50% interest in Peach Bottom 2 & 3 (~3,758 MW of nuclear capacity) selling energy, capacity and ancillary services into the PJM wholesale market. A third unit, PSEG Long Island, operates Long Island's T&D system under a fee-based Operations Services Agreement (OSA) with LIPA.

business_model.summary: PSE&G earns a regulated return on its rate base through BPU-approved distribution rates and FERC-approved transmission formula rates, with no commodity margin (supply costs pass through) and most distribution margin decoupled from sales volumes via the Conservation Incentive Program (CIP). PSEG Power earns largely market-based revenue from nuclear energy and PJM capacity auctions, partially buffered by a federal nuclear production tax credit (PTC, up to ~$15/MWh through 2032) that provides downside price protection. PSEG LI earns a fixed management/incentive fee plus pass-through cost reimbursement under its LIPA OSA (recently extended five years to 2030).

revenue_streams.name: Wholesale Electricity & Capacity Sales (PSEG Power, nuclear)
Wholesale Gas Sales (PSEG Power, incl. BGSS supply to PSE&G)
Other (appliance repair, solar, LIPA OSA fees, alternative revenues)

business_model.customer_type: Regulated B2C/B2B utility customer base (commercial ~57% of electric sales, residential 34%, industrial 9%) plus wholesale/institutional counterparties (PJM, LIPA) for the generation and OSA businesses
business_model.geographic_mix: Essentially 100% New Jersey for the regulated utility (PSE&G); nuclear generation fleet located in New Jersey and Pennsylvania selling into the PJM Interconnection (Mid-Atlantic); PSEG LI operates Long Island, NY T&D under contract

main_competitors: Constellation Energy (merchant nuclear fleet, spun from Exelon)
competitive_position.market_position: PSE&G holds an exclusive, state-franchised monopoly over electric and gas T&D in its New Jersey service territory. PSEG Power is one of the largest nuclear generators in PJM, with Salem/Hope Creek supplying over 80% of New Jersey's carbon-free power, giving it a prominent position among merchant nuclear operators (alongside Constellation, Vistra and Talen) competing for emerging large-load/data-center power contracts.

moat_factors.description: Exclusive BPU/FERC-franchised T&D service territory with rate-of-return regulation on ~$36 billion of rate base
Over 90% of PSE&G's electric and gas distribution margin is tied to customer counts, not usage, insulating earnings from efficiency gains or weather

moat_factors.factor: Large baseload nuclear fleet with policy support
moat_factors.description: ~3,758 MW of always-on, carbon-free nuclear generation with PTC downside protection through 2032 and multi-decade NRC license runway (2036-2066 across units), but exposed to PJM price volatility and single-unit operational risk

moat_factors.factor: FERC formula transmission rate with incentive adder
moat_factors.description: 9.90% base ROE plus a 50 bps RTO-membership adder provides predictable, trued-up annual transmission recovery, though the adder is now at risk from a new NJ mandatory-RTO-membership law and a pending FERC rulemaking

Incumbent transmission position and existing nuclear fleet give PSEG preferential access to PJM's capacity-constrained, data-center-driven demand growth versus new entrants facing long interconnection queues

weaknesses: Single-state regulatory concentration in New Jersey creates outsized exposure to one legislature/BPU/governor's political and affordability agenda
PSEG Power's merchant revenue is directly exposed to PJM/natural gas price swings and mark-to-market accounting volatility (GAAP EPS fell ~39% YoY in Q3 2026 largely on MTM losses)
Concentrated nuclear fleet (two sites) creates single-point-of-failure risk, illustrated by the October 2026 Salem Unit 1 thermal shield degradation extending its refueling outage indefinitely
Large multi-year capital program ($24-28 billion through 2030) carries execution, cost-overrun and regulatory-lag risk before costs are recovered in rates
Uncertainty over federal PTC/CAMT tax guidance (US Treasury has not finalized the 'gross receipts' definition) that could materially affect realized nuclear tax benefits

growth_drivers: Regulated rate base growth of 6.0%-7.5% CAGR (2025-2030) from a $24-28 billion five-year capital program (transmission, distribution reliability, Gas System Modernization Program III, Clean Energy Future-Energy Efficiency II, solar, EV infrastructure)

Data center/AI-driven load growth in PJM and New Jersey: PSEG's large-load interconnection pipeline has grown from ~400 MW in early 2024 to multiple gigawatts, driving incremental transmission and distribution capital needs and capacity-market revenue
Nuclear life extension and uprates: planned second license renewals (extending Salem to 2056/2060 and Hope Creek to 2066) and a ~200 MW Salem power uprate would add low-cost, carbon-free capacity
Potential long-term power sale agreements from the nuclear fleet to data centers/large power users, mirroring deals struck by Constellation, Vistra and Talen with hyperscalers
Record PJM capacity auction clearing prices (hitting the FERC price cap in the December 2025 auction) benefiting PSEG Power's existing nuclear capacity revenue
Electrification and decarbonization policy under New Jersey's updated Energy Master Plan (EVs, building electrification, grid modernization) supporting continued utility infrastructure investment

business.description: October 2026 discovery of thermal shield degradation at Salem Unit 1 is extending the refueling outage with an undetermined repair timeline and financial impact; the fleet's concentration in two sites raises correlated-outage risk

business.risk: Merchant power price and PJM capacity-market volatility
business.description: PSEG Power's results swing with natural gas prices, PJM energy/capacity clearing prices and non-trading mark-to-market gains/losses, as shown by the 39% YoY drop in Q3 2026 GAAP EPS

A $24-28 billion, multi-program capital plan (GSMP III, CEF-EE II, transmission) depends on timely permitting, supply chain, labor and BPU/FERC approvals; cost overruns or disallowances would depress realized returns

financial.description: Rising energy prices or loss of investment-grade ratings at PSEG Power would trigger materially higher letter-of-credit/cash collateral postings on hedges
Financial market declines could increase required contributions to defined-benefit and nuclear decommissioning trust funds
Heavy reliance on continuous external debt financing for the capital program; PSEG Power additionally needs investment-grade ratings to avoid large incremental collateral calls

regulatory.description: FERC's proposed elimination of the RTO-membership adder, now intertwined with a new NJ law mandating RTO membership by January 2027, could reduce PSE&G's annual net income by ~$40 million

New Jersey's new governor (took office January 2026) has directed the BPU to study utility business-model reform and mitigate rate increases; prior bill-credit settlements, a summer disconnection moratorium and extended payment plans have already raised bad-debt expense
U.S. Treasury has not finalized 'gross receipts' guidance for the nuclear production tax credit or fully clarified CAMT treatment; future guidance could be materially adverse or favorable

regulatory.risk: PJM/FERC capacity and large-load market redesign
regulatory.description: Ongoing FERC proceedings on the Reliability Backstop Procurement auction, co-located/large-load (data center) tariff rules, and capacity price caps create uncertainty for both PSE&G's cost pass-throughs and PSEG Power's capacity revenue

macro.description: Natural gas prices set the PJM marginal clearing price, directly affecting PSEG Power's realized energy margins above/below the PTC floor
Increasing frequency of storms raises restoration costs and capital needs, with recovery subject to regulatory approval
As a capital-intensive, debt-funded utility, PSEG's financing costs and equity valuation are sensitive to prevailing interest rates

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. regulated utilities face a historically strong capex/rate-base growth cycle driven by electrification, grid modernization and surging data center/AI electricity demand, particularly acute in the capacity-constrained PJM market where resource adequacy shortfalls have pushed capacity prices to record, FERC price-capped levels
macro_factors.cyclicality: PSE&G's regulated, decoupled T&D earnings are low-cyclicality and largely weather/economy-insensitive; PSEG Power's merchant nuclear earnings are more cyclical, tracking PJM energy and capacity price cycles and natural gas prices
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high: heavy reliance on debt to fund a $24-28 billion five-year capital program; PSE&G's transmission/distribution rate mechanisms partially offset financing-cost pass-through
key_input_costs: Natural gas (sets PJM marginal power price)

recent_developments.event: BPU approved PSE&G's GSMP III gas main replacement program ($1.05 billion) and released New Jersey's updated Energy Master Plan

New Jersey's new governor took office and issued executive orders directing the BPU to mitigate electric rate increases and study reform of the traditional utility business model; White House/13 PJM-state governors signed an agreement pushing PJM toward capacity market reform and a 15-year 'Reliability Backstop Procurement' auction

PSEG raised its 2026-2030 capital plan to $24-28 billion (regulated portion $22.5-25.5 billion) and reaffirmed 2026 non-GAAP operating EPS guidance of $4.28-$4.40 with a 6%-8% CAGR through 2030, citing accelerating data center/large-load demand

New Jersey enacted legislation mandating RTO membership for in-state transmission owners effective January 2027, creating a new path by which PSE&G's $40 million/year FERC RTO-membership ROE adder could be eliminated

PJM filed, and FERC partially rejected, proposed rules for a Reliability Backstop Procurement capacity auction and for curtailing large-load (data center) customers during peak demand, leaving PJM targeting a revised FERC filing and a March 2027 backstop auction

A visual inspection during Salem Unit 1's scheduled refueling outage found degradation to the reactor vessel's internal thermal shield, extending the outage with an unresolved repair timeline and financial impact

Q3 2026 results: non-GAAP operating EPS of $1.15 (+2% YoY) versus GAAP diluted EPS of $0.76 (down from $1.24 in Q3 2025), with the GAAP decline driven by mark-to-market losses on hedges and lower nuclear decommissioning trust gains; management reaffirmed full-year guidance

items.notes: Reaffirmed through Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 releases; FY2025 non-GAAP operating EPS was $4.05 (vs. $4.22 GAAP diluted EPS)
Long-term growth algorithm tied to regulated rate base growth

Raised in February 2026 (from a prior $22.5-$26 billion 2025-2029 plan) on accelerating data center/large-load demand and distribution reliability needs; expected to be funded internally without new common equity issuance
Includes the regulated program plus competitive transmission and other investments
From a base of ~$36 billion rate base at year-end 2025, up from ~$34 billion at year-end 2024

guidance.management_commentary: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance and the 2025-2030 6%-8% EPS growth algorithm despite the Q3 2026 GAAP earnings decline (attributed to MTM/NDT volatility, not core operations) and the unresolved Salem Unit 1 thermal-shield outage. CFO Daniel Cregg has attributed capital-plan increases to new large-load/data-center customer connections plus reliability and resilience upgrades, and emphasized the plan is funded without new equity issuance.

bull_case: Highly visible, BPU/FERC-sanctioned rate base growth of 6.0%-7.5% CAGR funds a 6%-8% EPS growth algorithm through 2030 without new equity dilution
Carbon-free nuclear fleet carries federal PTC downside protection through 2032 while retaining full upside from record PJM capacity and energy prices

New Jersey's data center/large-load interconnection pipeline has grown from ~400 MW to multiple gigawatts, creating a long runway of incremental, rate-based transmission/distribution investment plus optional nuclear PPA upside
Revenue decoupling (CIP) shields over 90% of PSE&G's distribution margin from weather and usage swings, giving defensive, utility-grade earnings visibility
Investment-grade balance sheet and internally-funded capital plan support continued dividend growth ($2.68/share indicated annual rate)
bear_case: Salem Unit 1's October 2026 thermal shield degradation underscores concentrated single-site/single-unit nuclear risk that can swing quarterly and potentially annual earnings

New Jersey's new governor and legislature are actively pursuing rate-affordability relief (bill credits, disconnection moratoria, a utility business-model study) that could compress allowed returns or slow cost recovery
PSEG Power's merchant earnings remain volatile, with GAAP EPS down ~39% YoY in Q3 2026 on mark-to-market losses, masking underlying operating trends from headline results

A newly enacted NJ law mandating RTO membership threatens PSE&G's $40 million/year FERC transmission ROE adder, and broader PJM/FERC capacity-market redesign (Reliability Backstop Procurement, large-load tariff rules) remains unresolved
Unresolved U.S. Treasury guidance on the nuclear PTC 'gross receipts' definition and CAMT treatment introduces material, unquantifiable tax uncertainty to PSEG Power's economics
